**Update (November 2026):** Added the 2025 and 2026 survey links and a current example. Survey findings describe respondents and should not be generalized to all developers without considering the methodology.

TL;DR The annual Stack Overflow Developer Survey is a snapshot of the developers who responded, not a census of the whole industry. It can suggest topics to investigate, but it should not determine a technology strategy on its own.

### How to Use the Survey

Survey results can help generate questions about tools, work habits, and learning needs. Interpret each finding in light of who responded, how the question was phrased, and whether the same question was asked in prior years.

For example, the [2026 technology results](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/technology/) report that 77% of surveyed developers build small scripts and automations. That is a result for the survey's respondents, not an estimate that should automatically be generalized to all developers or organizations.

Use findings to inform follow-up research:

- Compare survey results with your team's actual usage, constraints, and skills.
- Look for trends across multiple years only when questions and response options are comparable.
- Treat reported interest or usage as a signal to investigate, not proof of future adoption or product quality.
- Consider the survey's methodology and respondent profile before applying results to a different population.

### How to Access Stack Overflow Surveys

You can access the latest results and earlier surveys here:

- [Survey 2026](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/).
- [Survey 2025](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2025/).
- [Survey 2024](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/).  
- [Survey 2023](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2023/).  
- [Survey 2022](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2022/).  
- [Survey 2021](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2021/).  
- [Survey 2020](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2020/).  

When comparing years, check the survey documentation for changes to questions, sampling, and methodology.

### Conclusion

The survey is most useful as one input among many. Use it to identify broad signals, then validate them against your own users, organization, and independent evidence before making strategic decisions.
